prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet: a 4-frame SHIELD CHARGE animation of the KNIGHT, a slow, heavily armoured warrior behind a huge rune-carved tower shield, for a Doom/Hexen-style first-person game where monsters are drawn as sprites from several camera angles. The knight drops into a low crouch behind its shield and charges at the player STILL CROUCHED, pushing the shield ahead of it along the floor like a plough, the shield's bottom edge scraping the ground the whole way, and at the end slams it into a wall.

REFERENCE IMAGES, in the order attached:
1. The knight's turnaround sheet (front, front three-quarter, side, rear three-quarter, back). It is the character design: a broad humanoid in blackened, angular fantasy plate with spiked pauldrons, a closed HORNED HELM with two glowing pale-blue eyes in its narrow slit, steel tassets over dark chainmail, an all-metal TOWER SHIELD as tall as the knight (riveted rim, a central ridge, columns of carved runes glowing faint pale blue) on its LEFT arm, and a heavy flanged, spiked steel mace in its RIGHT hand. Also the shading style.
2. The knight standing, seen from THIS sheet's camera view. Match its camera angle, the way it faces, its pixel size, outline weight, scale and ground line exactly.

The shield stays on the left arm and the mace in the right hand in every frame. Never swap them, never draw a second shield, a second mace or a third arm. The horns, the glowing eyes and the runes look the same in every frame.

LAYOUT
- One horizontal row of 5 equal cells, read left to right, each cell as wide as reference 2: cell 1 the standing copy, cells 2 to 5 the 4 charge frames.
- Background: flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, with no gradient, texture, vignette, glow, cast shadow or floor.
- The cells are separated by thin vertical lines of pure cyan (#00FFFF), each running the full height of the image.
- Cell 1 is a plain copy of reference 2: the knight standing, exactly as tall, in exactly the same pose. It sets the scale for the other frames, which are drawn at the same scale.
- The feet stand on the same ground line in every cell, at the same height as in reference 2. The knight never hops or floats.
- The whole figure, including the horns, the shield and the mace, fits inside each cell with a clear magenta margin. Nothing touches a cell edge or a cyan line, and nothing is cropped.
- No text, labels, numbers, frame borders, speed lines, motion blur, smear trails, sparks, dust, blood, wall or impact effects. Only the knight.
- Crisp pixel art with hard edges and no anti-aliasing against the magenta. No semi-transparent pixels, and no pink or purple glow bleeding into the background.

THE CHARGE. Two things hold in every one of the 4 frames, and matter most:
- THE SHIELD IS DOWN ON THE GROUND. Its bottom edge rests ON the ground line, exactly level with the soles of the feet, never lifted above it. It stands upright, squarely in front of the body, covering it, and is pushed along the floor, not carried.
- THE KNIGHT IS CROUCHED, all four frames clearly lower than standing (about three quarters of reference 2's height, the horns near the shield's top rim): knees deeply bent, hips low, back hunched, the helm ducked behind the shield so only the horns and the glowing eyes show over its top rim, its shoulder braced against the shield's back. The mace is held back and low at the knight's right side, not swung.
- Frame 2 (cell 2), THE CROUCH, the warning before it runs: the knight sinks into the crouch behind the grounded shield, one foot set back to push off, coiled and still, the eyes blazing brighter. It is held a long moment, and must read at once as "about to charge".
- Frame 3 (cell 3), RUNNING CROUCHED, LEFT FOOT: still as low as frame 2, the whole body driving forward behind the shield, the left leg taking a short, heavy step forward under the body, the right leg straining back behind, pushing off from its toes. The shield's bottom edge stays on the ground.
- Frame 4 (cell 4), RUNNING CROUCHED, RIGHT FOOT: the same crouch, the same shield on the ground, the legs the other way: the right leg stepping forward, the left leg pushing off behind.
- Frame 5 (cell 5), THE CRASH: the instant the grounded shield slams into a wall in front of it: the knight jarred to a stop and bounced up and back out of its crouch, the shield knocked back against its body and tilted, its bottom edge still on the ground, the helm snapped back, the glowing eyes flaring, the mace arm flung a little wide, the legs splayed and staggering. It must read as a hard, dazed collision.
VIEW: side profile, as in the third cell of reference 1 and in reference 2. The knight faces IMAGE-LEFT in every cell; keep this profile, the body must not turn toward the viewer. The shield is held in front on the near arm, seen edge-on at the image-left side of the body; the mace hangs from the far arm.
In the walk the legs scissor clearly in profile, the near leg drawn in front where it passes. In the attack the mace swings in a big arc up behind the helm (toward image-right) and down in front (toward image-left), over the top of the shield.
In the charge from this angle: the knight crouches low behind the shield, leaning toward the way it faces, the shield ahead of it on that side with its bottom edge resting on the ground line; in the crash it rocks up and back away from that side.

REFERENCE IMAGE 3 is the finished animation seen from the FRONT, laid out the same way (cell 1 standing, then the frames). It is the same animation this sheet must show: the same poses, the same timing, the same arms. Only the camera angle changes, to the one in reference 2.
